items.name: Gull knife
items.flavor: A short blade, nicked from cutting weed and rope.
items.codexEntry: Nobody remembers who first called it the gull knife. It is small, quick and rude, which is how gulls are generally described.

items.name: Driftwood staff
items.flavor: Bleached, straight and surprisingly good for pointing.
items.codexEntry: A walking staff worn smooth by someone else’s hands. It is better at indicating the correct direction than at hitting anything.

items.name: Oar hook
items.flavor: Meant for catching boats. Catches other things.
items.codexEntry: A long iron hook on an ash pole, kept by every tidewarden for pulling in what the sea sends and pushing off what it shouldn’t.

items.name: Oilskin coat
items.flavor: Stiff, yellow and smelling faithfully of fish.
items.codexEntry: Waxed canvas, patched at both elbows. It turns rain, spray and the occasional opinion.

items.name: Salt lantern
items.codexEntry: The lantern from the Saltwick signal post. It is said to be warm because someone, somewhere, is thinking of whoever carries it.

items.name: Brine tonic
items.flavor: Tastes of the sea. Works anyway.
items.codexEntry: A cloudy tonic sold in stoppered bottles on the Saltwick quay. The recipe is a secret mainly because nobody wants to claim it.

items.name: Tarred sou’wester
items.flavor: Brimmed, stiff and still faintly damp from someone else’s day.
items.codexEntry: A sailor’s hat, tarred until it shed water the way a duck sheds opinions. This one has been hung on a causeway marker to dry for longer than the tar suggests.
